title: Ice cream parlor, Sunday Black bands and Tremé halls
summary: Non-musical family; father's ice cream parlor near Economy Hall and the Tremé market where bands advertised dances.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh... Whatever you... Wherever you want to start telling about your life. You know, did you come from a musical family? No. Nobody played music in front of you?
No. They all were hardworking folks. I mean, ice cream business. My dad was an ice cream business.
Well, that gave you an opportunity to hear a little music, I guess, huh?

Oh, yeah. I mean, uh... You told me. It was at the corner of my house there. The old man had an ice cream parlor there. And every Sunday there would be some Negro bands there. They would sort of meet each other and, you know, buck each other.

And they would advertise for, like, dances and so forth. But it was, like, picnics or sales or something like that. And then they had these dances at night there at the economy hall of the center centers. And then they had the Astoria, the Capellet, you know, all those old halls, you know? Where were you going? Well, on St. Anne between, uh, Morewa and Liberty, just back at the auditorium, they had that old tone on since.
Yeah, the Tremé Market. Yeah. There was a big open market there.
Yeah. And where was your daddy's ice cream place? It was on St. Philip and North Billeray.

Well, you never did move much away from that. No, and then after we had moved in the middle of the block, which was around, uh, let's see, between, uh, North Robison and North, you know, Burberry. All St. Philip Street, but in the middle of the block. And, uh, he got a big place there and he expanded some.
So you were close to Economy Hall and...
Yeah, I was up around the corner from the, uh, and around the corner from the Center Center. Yeah. And about a few blocks from the Interpreseverance. Mm-hmm.
And you heard the bands, didn't you? Oh, yeah, I heard a lot of them. Did you have any neighbors who played music that you used to listen to?
